summary: An unchanged harness.observed report (a re-stamp) stays in the node's local observation log once every other member hears its seats from its seat_freshness pushes; until then one replicates every five minutes instead of every minute

replay.detail: Fewer harness.observed claims are written. A report whose fields other than observed_at_ms, observed_since_ms and status_transition match the latest replicated one stays local while this node's meta key fleet_hears_seats is 1, unless readers would otherwise fold the seat to something newer than it (work activity after a resting report). The seat freshness pusher sets the key at each round, which a commit wakes: 1 when every other current member, or configured peer, advertises seat_freshness in its own daemon.started and this node's last push reached it, and this node is not a dial-out member; a member no push can reach (no direct route, such as a dial-out member, or a worker without the route) keeps it 0; a node outside a fleet sets it to 1. While it is 0 or unset, an unchanged report replicates when the replicated one is at least five minutes old, for working and legacy posters alike. Transitions and field changes replicate as before. Old claims are untouched.

schema.detail: No schema change: fleet_hears_seats is a node-local meta key, which never replicates.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Contract C3 of the claims-store breakup (approved). Remote seat freshness comes from the seat's host: its own cards read its local log, and other members read its seat_freshness pushes. An older member, which reads report ages, keeps every host it can see on the five-minute fallback, inside its 661-second down rule; its cards read a resting remote seat as stale after 90 seconds, as they already do for resting native seats. The host's wake acknowledgement reads its local log, so a working re-stamp after a wake still counts. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI shape changes. Two follow-ups to the seat freshness push: a pushed time later than the receiver's clock plus 60 seconds is taken as that, so a host whose clock runs ahead cannot keep a seat looking fresh; and a bound harness calling the daemon's /v1/internal/seat-freshness is refused, as every internal route now refuses seat callers (#4433); a test pins it for this route.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting replicates an unchanged report once a minute again while the seat works; the local log holds every report meanwhile.
